_comment: The hook block SpriteRoom writes into ~/.claude/settings.json on first run,
with consent. Registered once at user scope, matcher '*', so it covers every
project and routes by cwd — see docs/02-ARCHITECTURE.md.
Only the ten events docs/03-EVENT-MODEL.md consumes are registered. Every
other event Claude Code emits is deliberately NOT registered: an unregistered
event costs the user nothing, and the listener still decodes anything that
does arrive to .unhandled rather than throwing.
'type': 'http' is native — the session POSTs the hook input JSON straight to
the URL, no shim script. Verified against Claude Code 2.1.224; see
docs/FINDINGS-M0.md.
There is no 'async' field on the HTTP hook schema. The session BLOCKS on our
response. A listener holding for 3s was measured adding 3s to every tool call
in the session. That is the entire reason for I5 — respond 202 and return.
'timeout' is a floor under our own failure: if SpriteRoom is not running, or
wedges, the user's session stalls by at most this long per event. Keep it low.
The port is rewritten from the app's config at install time.
PostToolBatch carries no matcher, unlike the rest. That is the shape it was
captured working under, and it is the only close path for a permission-denied
call — so it is the last entry to get clever with. Do not add a matcher to it
without re-capturing and confirming it still fires.
